course: NISM Series II-B: Registrars to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents - Mutual Fund
overview: This unit is the 'Standard Operating Procedure' (SOP) manual for an RTA. It explains the technical 'pipes' through which money and data flow. You will learn about Folios (your digital locker), the importance of PAN and KYC (your identity), and the 'Cut-off time' rules that decide which day's price (NAV) an investor gets. For the NISM exam, this chapter is high-stakes because it covers the mandatory legal requirements you must check before clicking the 'Process' button on any transaction.

complete_concept_explanation.concept: 1. The Folio Number (Your Mutual Fund Account)
complete_concept_explanation.basic_meaning: A Folio is a unique account number given by the RTA to an investor. It is like a 'folder' that stores all your different investments in one place.
complete_concept_explanation.detailed_explanation:
When an investor first puts money into an AMC, the RTA generates a 'Folio Number'. 
Step 1: One Folio per AMC. Usually, if you invest in 5 different schemes of SBI Mutual Fund, they will all be under one single Folio number. 
Step 2: Multiple Holders. A folio can be held by one person (Single), or up to three people (Jointly). 
Step 3: Ownership Proof. The Folio is the final proof of ownership. Even if the investor loses their statement, as long as the RTA has the Folio record, the money is safe.
complete_concept_explanation.why_this_is_important: As an RTA, you spend your whole day searching for and updating 'Folios'. Understanding that one folio can hold multiple schemes is basic but critical.
complete_concept_explanation.real_life_indian_example: If you have an HDFC Flexi Cap Fund and an HDFC Liquid Fund, you don't need two account numbers. Both will appear under the same HDFC Folio (e.g., Folio No. 12345/67).
exam_traps: Trap: 'Can an investor have only one folio across all Indian mutual funds?' NO. Each AMC gives its own folio. You will have a different folio for ICICI and a different one for HDFC.
Remember that a folio can have a maximum of 3 joint holders.
complete_concept_explanation.memory_trick: Folio = Folder. One folder stores many papers (schemes) from the same office (AMC).

complete_concept_explanation.basic_meaning: PAN (Permanent Account Number) and KYC (Know Your Customer) are mandatory identity checks. Without these, no one can invest in a mutual fund in India.
complete_concept_explanation.detailed_explanation:
To prevent money laundering (black money), SEBI has made these rules: 
1. PAN is Mandatory: Every investor (except for some very specific exceptions like Micro-SIPs up to Rs. 50,000) must provide their PAN card. 
2. KYC Compliance: KYC is a one-time process where the RTA or a KRA (KYC Registration Agency) verifies the investor's Identity Proof (like Aadhaar/PAN) and Address Proof. 
3. KRA: Once you do your KYC with one mutual fund, the data is stored in a central 'KRA' database. You don't have to do it again for the next mutual fund.
complete_concept_explanation.why_this_is_important: The RTA is the 'Police' here. If an application comes without a PAN or if the KYC is 'Rejected', the RTA must reject the investment and refund the money.
complete_concept_explanation.real_life_indian_example: If you try to buy a fund on an app, it first checks your PAN. If it says 'KYC Verified', you can invest. If not, the RTA's system will block your purchase until you upload your Aadhaar and a photo.
exam_traps: Is there any exemption for PAN? Yes, only for 'Micro-SIPs' where the total investment in a year is less than Rs. 50,000. But even then, 'PAN-exempt KYC' is still needed.
Who maintains the central KYC data? It is the KRAs (like CVL, CAMS KRA), not the AMC.
complete_concept_explanation.memory_trick: No PAN, No Plan. No KYC, No Buy.

complete_concept_explanation.concept: 3. Cut-off Time and Applicable NAV (The Clock Rule)
complete_concept_explanation.basic_meaning: The 'Cut-off Time' is the deadline each day. If you invest before this time, you get today's price. If you invest after this time, you get tomorrow's price.
complete_concept_explanation.detailed_explanation:
Since NAV is calculated at the end of the day, SEBI has fixed a 'Cut-off time' (usually 3:00 PM) to ensure fairness. 
[Image illustrating the cut-off time rules for mutual fund transactions]
Rule 1: Purchase (Other than Liquid): If money and application reach the RTA before 3:00 PM AND the funds are 'available for use' by the AMC, the investor gets the same day's NAV. 
Rule 2: Redemption (Selling): If the request reaches the RTA before 3:00 PM, the investor gets the same day's closing NAV. 
Rule 3: Liquid Funds: These have a stricter cut-off (usually 1:30 PM) and a special rule: If you invest before 1:30 PM, you get the PREVIOUS day's NAV (to give you the benefit of today's interest).
complete_concept_explanation.why_this_is_important: This is the most common cause of investor complaints. RTAs must timestamp every application to prove exactly when it was received. A 1-minute delay can change the price the investor pays.
complete_concept_explanation.step_by_step_calculation_example:
Step 1: Investor submits a purchase form for an Equity Fund at 2:45 PM on Monday.
Step 2: The money is also transferred instantly.
Step 3: Result: They get Monday's NAV.
Step 4: If they submit at 3:05 PM on Monday, they get Tuesday's NAV.
complete_concept_explanation.real_life_indian_example: During a market crash, everyone wants to buy. If the Nifty falls 5% on Monday, and you want that low price, you MUST ensure your application and money reach the RTA's system before 3:00 PM on Monday.
exam_traps: The most important rule now is 'Realization of Funds'. Even if you apply at 10:00 AM, if your bank sends the money to the AMC only at 4:00 PM, you will NOT get today's NAV. You will get the NAV of the day when the money is actually received.
Liquid funds have a 1:30 PM cut-off, while others have 3:00 PM.
complete_concept_explanation.memory_trick: Before 3 = Today's Price. After 3 = Tomorrow's Price.

complete_concept_explanation.concept: 4. Transaction Types: SIP, STP, and SWP
complete_concept_explanation.basic_meaning: These are 'Automated' ways to move your money, designed by RTAs to make investing easy.
complete_concept_explanation.detailed_explanation:
1. SIP (Systematic Investment Plan): Automatically investing a fixed amount (e.g., Rs. 1,000) every month. The RTA manages the 'Mandate' which tells the bank to send money every month.
2. STP (Systematic Transfer Plan): Automatically moving money from one scheme (e.g., Liquid fund) to another (e.g., Equity fund) within the same AMC. This is great for 'Rupee Cost Averaging'.
3. SWP (Systematic Withdrawal Plan): The opposite of SIP. You automatically take out a fixed amount every month. Great for pensioners who want a 'Monthly Salary' from their investments.
complete_concept_explanation.why_this_is_important: RTAs are the engines for these. When you set an STP, the RTA's computer system automatically 'sells' from Fund A and 'buys' in Fund B on the 5th of every month without you doing anything.
complete_concept_explanation.real_life_indian_example: If you have Rs. 12 Lakhs and don't want to invest it all at once in the risky stock market, you put it in a Liquid Fund and start an STP of Rs. 1 Lakh per month into an Equity Fund. The RTA will do this 12-month job for you automatically.
exam_traps: Does a SIP guarantee profits? NO. It only averages your cost of purchase.
STP only works between schemes of the SAME Mutual Fund (AMC). You cannot STP from SBI to HDFC.
complete_concept_explanation.memory_trick: SIP = Inflow (Buying). SWP = Outflow (Selling). STP = Transfer (Shifting).

important_differences.clear_explanation: Purchase is when an investor gives money to the AMC and receives 'Units' from the RTA. Redemption is when the investor gives 'Units' back to the RTA and receives 'Money' from the AMC.

Individual investors are humans (Single or Joint). Non-individual investors are 'Entities' like Companies, Trusts, or HUFs. The KYC documents and signing authority rules are much stricter for Non-individuals.
Lumpsum is a one-time investment (e.g., investing Rs. 50,000 today). SIP is a recurring investment (e.g., Rs. 5,000 every month for 10 months).

frequently_asked_exam_areas: The 3:00 PM Cut-off rule and 'Realization of Funds' condition (Mandatory for all purchases).
Maximum number of joint holders allowed in a folio (3).
Exemption limit for Micro-SIPs from PAN (Rs. 50,000 per year per AMC).
Who is responsible for KYC? (KRAs - KYC Registration Agencies).
quick_revision_summary: A Folio is your unique account number; one folio can hold many schemes of the same AMC.
PAN and KYC are mandatory for almost all mutual fund investments in India.
To get today's NAV, your application AND your money must reach the AMC/RTA before 3:00 PM.
Liquid funds have a 1:30 PM cut-off and can provide the previous day's NAV.
SIP (Buying), SWP (Selling), and STP (Transferring) are the three main automated transaction types.
RTAs use 'Time-stamping' machines to prove when an application was received.
A maximum of 3 people can jointly hold a mutual fund folio.
